comment: For a 101 course, it wasn't completely easy, but I believe the workload and standards are manageable. If you put in the effort and communicate, you're more likely to succeed, but he can be a harsh grader. You can skip out on the readings and still write out all the papers. Interesting class that will have you thinking, but also have you working.

Don't take this class, at least not with him. Lectures are so boring and papers have nothing to do with the material. If your viewpoints don't align, oh boy are you in for a treat. This guy is out of his mind, gives awful feedback, and would rather be smoking outside like he does before every single class. Do yourself a favor and stay away.

Please do not take this class. He gives you no rubric, terrible grades, and honestly everyone ends up with a B, even if you do well on the papers. Your grade is comprised on 3 Memos, two papers, and participation. Its on a point system out of 100 so if you loose 5 points on an essay your already down to a 95. Do not take. Waste of time.

Honestly never understood his grading, he was nice but his lectures were all over the place. You write 5 short papers, but none of them relate so feedback he writes on the one can't be used on others. The final paper is 12+ pages but no tests ever. You will never be as specific as he wants and expects you to know random facts you would never know.

Loved this class! So interesting and would take it again if I could, he knows so much about so many things and I genuinely looked forward to coming to class. The memos were a bit confusing at first, but overall he just wants in-depth concise work.

As an actual class, it was not the greatest - there is little to determine your grade and I'm still unsure how he grades papers. However, I found myself excited for every class. He is a fascinating professor that knows an awful lot about his subject and I found his class extremely interesting. I have learnt more in his class than in any other.

Professor Hass is a good professor who is very knowledgeable about the area; however, his teaching style isn't for everyone. The class is very lecture heavy and he assigns quite a bit of reading, but not all of needs to be read to be fair. The grading system isn't the best as you're graded on just a few essays, but there is no quizzes nor tests.

I took Global Studies 251 with him. He definitely likes to talk. Ain't the kind of prof you want to grab a beer with but he is very knowledgable about his subjects. Kinda all over the place and I feel he tried to get too specific on too many topics. Gives 100-page readings every class but I almost never read them and it was fine.
Such a boring class. Lectures are so all over the place. Your grade is solely based off 3 papers. Definitely don't take this as an FYS, such a waste of time and hurts your GPA>
Is not clear on what he wants in your papers. Grade was based on very few essays and nothing else really. Lectures are more like rambling. Not helpful when approached for help.

Do not take Hass. All he does is lecture, and it's overly rehearsed and boring. He doesn't even bring up 50+ page reading assignments during class. All his feedback on my papers was negative, and I didn't even get a bad grade, he's just mean. He obviously knows a lot about sociology, but he talks like he needs to prove he's smarter than you.

His lectures were genuinely so interesting and really changed the way I view everything. He is so intelligent about literally everything, sometimes too intelligent, but always found a way to convey the message to students. So thought-provoking. Lots of assigned readings but not necessary for class, just shove a few quotes in your papers.

Gives good lectures that are interesting but final grade depends on too few assignments. His grading criteria for the papers are extremely vague which makes it nearly impossible to get an A in the class. The workload however is fairly light and is good if you need the gen ed. However, if you care about your GPA i would recommend against this class.

One of the worst classes I have ever taken, I may as well of listened to a podcast. He just talks at you the entire time and no one pays attentions. He gives you the notes, so you literally do not have to do anything. Good class to take to fill credit or to have dedicated time to online shop.

Dr. Hass is clearly very intelligent but a little to his detriment. He does not always understand when the class is confused. If you're taking his Socialism FYS, it is very heavy on group discussion and there is tons of reading. However, I did like him and he is a fascinating professor and pretty funny.

Insanely hard readings of 50+ pages needed for every class. Content is confusing and difficult to even grasp. Grading is arbitrary. The majority of the grade is a final paper and participation, neither of which grades are given to you at the end of the semester, meaning your grade can be made or broken on a whim.

He knows his stuff, but I think he forgets we do not. The grade was based on three "reflections" (essays), the final paper, and participation. You will learn a lot in this class, but be ready to read 50-100 pages per night (can scrape by w out reading), whether you read or not, you will likely be confused--but after all, it is theory.

Dr. Hass is a brilliant professor. However, the class was difficult & expectations for papers were often very vague. The assigned readings were never discussed in class & I often found myself leaving class w/ more questions than answers. If you're a strong writer who is willing to put in the effort, take Hass - he'll definitely get you thinking.

Dr. Hass is pretty funny and cool guy to talk to about a wide range of topics. However, the class content was very unfocused and lacked clear takeaways. He didnt even mention most of our reading assignments, so many were a big waste of time. I dont think most students really absorbed any information, but we had some interesting discussions.

Hass gives AMAZING lectures. Get past the weird throat thing he does, and you'll be amazed by the things he has to say. Gives off evil genius vibes in the best way possible. If you don't go to class, you should still be able to do the assignments pretty well. Readings aren't really discussed in class, so those aren't really mandatory. Take Hass!!
Great professor. Definitely more difficult than many alternatives but worth taking.
Great lectures. Makes you think

Among the worst professors at UR. I had him for 2 classes in 1 semester and he spent more time trying to take shots at conservatives than teaching the material. If you are conservative at all about hass.

I had very low expectations coming into his FYS. The only reason I took it was because it was the the only one available but it was the best course I have taken at Richmond. He is the single most engaging professor that I have ever taken. His class is hard and very time consuming but if you do the work it is very rewarding class.
Dr. Hass is ok. He's not a bad professor but he is not great. He loves the topic so the passion definitely keeps it interesting.

Professor Hass demands a lot of his students, specifically of his 101 level course. The reading is necessary for the papers alone, at least the important parts of the books used, but his lectures are significantly more helpful, so attending class is very useful. He plans to shock you and doesn't provide any sort of solution/fix, be prepared.

Proffesor Hass is a damn good teacher....but I would have to say he is majorly weird kind of loopy but he knows what the hell he is talking about....he also does this wierd cough every 4-8 seconds i think it could be tourettes or something...I always contemplated asking him what is was during class...other than that he is a great teacher!!
Such a great teacher. Makes the content fun and interesting. Such a funny teacher. I really enjoy his class so much.

Class is mostly entirely lecture, with little chance for student discussion. But Dr. Hass is a great lecturer, you can tell he really knows his stuff. Fair grader. Alot of reading but minimal papers. Doesn't take attendance & it seems like he doesn't really care if you show up for class. Therefore a few students come to like every fifth class.

Class consists of lectures and weekly discussion (online and in class). He grades according to effort and thought and uses real world examples rather than just explaining the theories. Great class, I would definitely recommend it, might be a little depressing but it makes you think about the world completely differently. You can tell Hass loves it.

Brilliant prof, I strongly recommend him for Intro to Soc. He has his students read interesting books and excerpts rather than teaching by a text book. He makes this subject interesting and relevant. Most importantly, he always encourages meeting with him outside of class. Great to talk to.

Hass is a great prof - I highly recommend him for intro to Soc. His style is lecture dominated - but he is so interesting that you're never bored. He is helpful, and more concerned with you learning the material tahn the grade. His class consists of 2 big papers and 5 short journal style memos. A very duable, interesting class.

Had Dr. Hass for the 101 class. He is extremely knowledgeable, and does a pretty good job at making points clear and answering questions. He expects a lot from his students, but is always more than willing to help and meet with you. His lectures are always entertaining and interesting. Definitely among the better professors at UR.
God's gift to education.
